subject: black widow spider
title: Spiders Kill Snakes 30 Times Their Weight, and Win 86% of the Time

scenes.text: Spiders eat snakes. On every continent but one.
In 2021 two zoologists collected every record they could find. 319 cases of spiders killing snakes, from the United States to Australia.
The snakes averaged 26 centimeters. The longest, a meter-long green snake in Florida, taken by a golden silk orb-weaver.
Nearly a third of the snakes were venomous: coral snakes, rattlesnakes, lanceheads. The spiders won 86 percent of the time.
About half the kills were widow spiders. Their venom is tuned to vertebrates, and their silk holds a snake 30 times their weight while it works.
Then the spider feeds for days. The one continent with no record is Antarctica, which has no snakes.

description:
Spiders kill and eat snakes, including venomous ones, on every continent except Antarctica.
A 2021 review in the Journal of Arachnology by Martin Nyffeler and Whitfield Gibbons gathered 319 records of spiders preying on snakes. The snakes averaged about 26 cm, with the largest around a meter; nearly a third were venomous species such as coral snakes and rattlesnakes. The spider attack was fatal in 86 percent of cases. Widow spiders accounted for roughly half the kills, overpowering snakes 10 to 30 times their size with silk and a venom that is highly potent against vertebrates.
Which animal matchup would you least expect the smaller one to win?
first_comment: About half the records came from the United States and nearly a third from Australia; Europe had fewer than one percent. Have you ever seen a spider take something much bigger than itself?
